title: Map of Arabia, the Red Sea and Abyssinia
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Written for islamic-studies/y4 lesson 15 (Pupil PDF worksheet: map of Arabia, the Red Sea and Abyssinia)
intro: Lesson 15: The Hijrah to Abyssinia and the just king. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: A safe place
points: The Prophet ﷺ told some Muslims to go to Abyssinia
Its king was known to be just
They crossed the Red Sea, about 615 CE

panels.title: The Quraysh follow
points: Two Quraysh envoys brought gifts to the king
They asked him to send the Muslims back
The king said: first I will hear them

panels.title: Ja'far speaks
points: We used to worship idols and do wrong
Allah sent a messenger who taught truth

blocks.h: Map: Makkah, the Red Sea and Abyssinia

blocks.text: Label the Red Sea between Arabia and Africa. Draw an arrow for the journey.

keywords.def: moving to another place for the sake of Allah
a kingdom in Africa, around modern Ethiopia
the title of the just king of Abyssinia

questions.q: Explain why the Muslims went to Abyssinia.
questions.a: They were being hurt in Makkah; the Prophet ﷺ sent them to a just king who would protect them.

questions.q: On the pupil PDF map, mark Makkah, the Red Sea and Abyssinia, then write three sentences: why they left, what Ja'far said, what the king did.
questions.a: Correct map; three sentences on persecution, Ja'far's speech and the king's protection

questions.q: Extend: what did the king do before deciding?
questions.a: He listened to both the envoys and the Muslims.

questions.q: Stretch: what makes a ruler just? Give two features.
questions.a: Listens to both sides; protects the weak; does not take bribes

questions.q: Why did the king let the Muslims stay?
questions.a: A) He listened and was just. He heard both sides and judged fairly.

questions.q: Think again: what was hardest for those Muslims to leave, and why did they go?
questions.a: Family and home; to keep their faith safe.
